overall: The AG found the Wayland School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by giving notice of an interim superintendent appointment only by title, without naming the candidate; the remote-member announcement claim was rejected.

allegations.summary: Notice of the October 24 meeting should have named the acting superintendent candidate for interim appointment, not just listed the position title.
allegations.key_passage: As the Committee failed to list David Fleishman as a candidate under consideration for the position of Interim Superintendent, it violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Chair allegedly did not clearly announce the names of members attending the October 24 meeting remotely.
allegations.key_passage: The announcement may have been rushed but it cannot be said that it was not clearly audible.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law’s requirements and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
